links.outcome: Performance of derivation-hospital models on temporal and external hospitals (dataset shift)
links.effect: Temporal validation median AUROC fell to 0.65 NAM, 0.73 RAM, 0.67 YIM vs original 0.76, 0.84, 0.79. External validation showed similar findings with hospital-level variation.
links.quote: Temporal validation demonstrated reduced discrimination across all 3 models (median AUROC, 0.65 [95% CI 0.62-0.67] for the NAM; 0.73 [95% CI 0.72-0.75) for RAM; 0.67 [95% CI 0.63-0.70) for the YIM compared with the original estimates (median AUROC 0.76 [95% CI 0.85-0.78] for the NAM; 0.84 [95% CI 0.83-0.84] for the RAM; 0.79 [95% CI 0.77-0.80] for the YIM).

links.outcome: Calibration and discrimination of models at other hospitals versus developer estimates
links.effect: Only 3 hospitals for RAM (6.4%) and 9 for NAM and YIM (19.1%) were adequately calibrated; most hospitals had over- or underestimation of risk.
links.quote: Of 47 other PHIS hospitals, only 3 for the RAM (6.4%) and 9 for both the NAM and YIM (19.1%) were adequately calibrated.

links.outcome: Variation in model AUROC across hospitals
links.effect: External validation median (range) AUROC 0.64 (0.60-0.68) NAM, 0.73 (0.64-0.80) RAM, 0.65 (0.53-0.74) YIM, showing demonstrable variation across hospitals.
links.quote: External validation yielded similiar findings as the temporal validation, although with demonstrable variation in performance across hospitals (median [range] AUROC, 0.64 [0.60-0.68] for the NAM; 0.73 [0.64-0.80] for the RAM; 0.65 [0.53-0.74] for the YIM).

links.outcome: Temporal degradation of model discrimination from derivation period to 2019
links.effect: Median AUROC declined across all three models in temporal validation, e.g., NAM 0.76 to 0.65, RAM 0.84 to 0.73, YIM 0.79 to 0.67.
links.quote: This prognostic study found that the readmission risk prediction models had reduced predictive accuracy across time and variability in hospital-level performance.

screen.reason: The study conducts multi-site temporal and external validation across 48 hospitals evaluating performance drift and calibration of pediatric readmission risk models, but does not compare outcomes with vs without an organizational deployment practice.
